title: Wave Optics
syllabus: Wave front and Huygens' principle, reflection and refraction of plane wave at a plane surface using wave fronts; Proof of laws of reflection and refraction using Huygens' principle; Interference, Young's double slit experiment and expression for fringe width, coherent sources and sustained interference of light; Diffraction due to a single slit, width of central maximum; Resolving power of microscopes and astronomical telescopes; Polarisation, plane polarised light, Brewster's law, uses of plane polarised light and Polaroids

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] In Young's double slit experiment, if the separation between the slits is halved and the distance between the slits and the screen is doubled, the fringe width will:
questions.solution:
Fringe width in YDSE is given by $\beta = \frac{\lambda D}{d}$.
When slit separation is halved ($d' = d/2$) and distance to screen is doubled ($D' = 2D$):
$$\beta' = \frac{\lambda D'}{d'} = \frac{\lambda(2D)}{d/2} = 4\left(\frac{\lambda D}{d}\right) = 4\beta$$
Hence, the fringe width becomes four times its initial value.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] In a Young's double slit experiment, the ratio of maximum to minimum intensity in the interference fringe pattern is $25 : 9$. The ratio of the slit widths $w_1 : w_2$ is:
questions.solution:
Ratio of intensities:
$$\frac{I_{\max}}{I_{\min}} = \left(\frac{A_1 + A_2}{A_1 - A_2}\right)^2 = \frac{25}{9} \implies \frac{A_1 + A_2}{A_1 - A_2} = \frac{5}{3}$$
$$3A_1 + 3A_2 = 5A_1 - 5A_2 \implies 2A_1 = 8A_2 \implies \frac{A_1}{A_2} = 4$$
Since slit width $w$ is proportional to intensity $I \propto A^2$:
$$\frac{w_1}{w_2} = \frac{I_1}{I_2} = \left(\frac{A_1}{A_2}\right)^2 = 4^2 = 16 : 1$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] In a single slit diffraction experiment, light of wavelength $600\text{ nm}$ illuminates a slit of width $0.2\text{ mm}$. The linear width of the central diffraction maximum on a screen placed $2.0\text{ m}$ away is:
questions.solution:
Linear width of the central diffraction maximum is:
$$\beta_0 = \frac{2\lambda D}{a}$$
Substitute $\lambda = 600 \times 10^{-9}\text{ m}$, $D = 2.0\text{ m}$, and $a = 0.2 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}$:
$$\beta_0 = \frac{2 \times (600 \times 10^{-9}) \times 2.0}{0.2 \times 10^{-3}} = \frac{2400 \times 10^{-9}}{0.2 \times 10^{-3}} = 1.2 \times 10^{-2}\text{ m} = 12.0\text{ mm}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] An unpolarised light beam of intensity $I_0$ passes through two polaroids whose transmission axes are inclined at an angle of $60^\circ$ to each other. The intensity of light transmitted through the second polaroid is:
questions.solution:
Intensity transmitted by the first polaroid from unpolarised light is $I_1 = \frac{I_0}{2}$.
By Malus's Law, intensity transmitted by the second polaroid is:
$$I_2 = I_1 \cos^2\theta = \left(\frac{I_0}{2}\right) \cos^2(60^\circ) = \frac{I_0}{2} \times \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{I_0}{8}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] In a Young's double slit experiment, a transparent mica sheet of thickness $t$ and refractive index $\mu$ is introduced in the path of one of the interfering beams. The shift of the central fringe pattern on the screen is:
questions.solution:
Introducing a sheet of thickness $t$ and refractive index $\mu$ introduces an extra optical path length $\Delta x = (\mu - 1)t$.
For the central bright fringe, the net path difference is zero: $d\left(\frac{y_0}{D}\right) - (\mu - 1)t = 0$.
$$y_0 = \frac{D}{d}(\mu - 1)t$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The wavefront corresponding to a parallel beam of light propagating in a homogeneous medium is:
questions.solution:
A wavefront is the locus of all points having the same phase of oscillation.
For a parallel beam of light (such as light originating from a source at infinity), the rays are mutually parallel and perpendicular to a family of flat planes, yielding a planar wavefront.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] Two coherent monochromatic light sources have an intensity ratio $\frac{I_1}{I_2} = 4$. In their interference pattern, the visibility of fringes defined as $V = \frac{I_{\max} - I_{\min}}{I_{\max} + I_{\min}}$ is:
[JEE Main 2023] A beam of unpolarised light is incident at the polarising angle $\theta_p$ on a glass surface of refractive index $\mu = 1.732$. The value of $\theta_p$ is:
questions.solution:
According to Brewster's law:
$$\tan\theta_p = \mu$$
Given $\mu = 1.732 = \sqrt{3}$:
$$\tan\theta_p = \sqrt{3} \implies \theta_p = 60^\circ$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] In a Young's double slit experiment using light of wavelength $\lambda = 500\text{ nm}$, the $4^{\text{th}}$ bright fringe coincides with the $5^{\text{th}}$ dark fringe of another light of wavelength $\lambda'$. The wavelength $\lambda'$ is:
questions.solution:
Position of the $4^{\text{th}}$ bright fringe: $y_4 = 4\frac{\lambda D}{d}$.
Position of the $5^{\text{th}}$ dark fringe: $y'_5 = \left(5 - \frac{1}{2}\right)\frac{\lambda' D}{d} = 4.5\frac{\lambda' D}{d}$.
Equating positions:
$$4\frac{\lambda D}{d} = 4.5\frac{\lambda' D}{d} \implies 4\lambda = 4.5\lambda'$$
$$\lambda' = \frac{4}{4.5}\lambda = \frac{8}{9}(500\text{ nm}) = \frac{4000}{9}\text{ nm} \approx 444.4\text{ nm}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] In a single slit Fraunhofer diffraction pattern, the angular spread of the central maximum is:
questions.solution:
The first minima on either side of the central maximum occur at angle $\theta$ given by $a\sin\theta = \pm\lambda \implies \theta \approx \pm\frac{\lambda}{a}$.
The total angular width of the central maximum is the angular distance between the two first-order minima:
$$2\theta = \frac{2\lambda}{a}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] According to Rayleigh's criterion for resolution, two point objects viewed through an aperture of diameter $D$ are just resolved when their angular separation is at least:
questions.solution:
Rayleigh's criterion states that two point sources are just resolved when the central diffraction maximum of one source falls on the first minimum of the other.
For a circular aperture of diameter $D$:
$$\theta_{\min} = \frac{1.22\lambda}{D}$$

questions.question: Which of the following optical phenomena conclusively confirms the transverse nature of electromagnetic light waves?
questions.solution:
Interference, diffraction, and refraction occur in both longitudinal waves (sound) and transverse waves.
Only transverse waves, whose vibrations occur perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation, can be restricted to a single plane of oscillation (polarised).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] In Young's double slit experiment, if the entire apparatus is immersed in water of refractive index $\mu = 4/3$, the fringe width $\beta'$ will be:
questions.solution:
In a medium of refractive index $\mu$, the wavelength decreases to $\lambda' = \frac{\lambda}{\mu}$.
Fringe width:
$$\beta' = \frac{\lambda' D}{d} = \frac{\lambda D}{\mu d} = \frac{\beta}{\mu} = \frac{\beta}{4/3} = \frac{3}{4}\beta$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Two independent light bulbs of the same wattage and color placed side by side do not produce an observable interference pattern because:
options: They are mutually incoherent sources with random, rapidly varying phase differences
The emitted light is strictly longitudinal
questions.solution:
To observe sustained interference, the light sources must be mutually coherent (maintaining a constant phase difference).
Independent thermal light sources emit light packets from independent atomic transitions at random intervals ($10^{-8}\text{ s}$), leading to random and rapidly changing phase relations that wash out any stationary interference fringes.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] The path difference between two interfering waves at a point on the screen is $\frac{\lambda}{6}$. If $I_0$ is the maximum intensity at the central bright fringe, the intensity at this point is:
questions.solution:
Phase difference for a path difference $\Delta x = \frac{\lambda}{6}$ is:
$$\phi = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}\Delta x = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}\left(\frac{\lambda}{6}\right) = \frac{\pi}{3}$$
Intensity formula for two equal interfering beams:
$$I = I_0 \cos^2\left(\frac{\phi}{2}\right) = I_0 \cos^2\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right) = I_0 \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{3}{4} I_0$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The limit of resolution of a telescope with an objective lens of diameter $D$ using light of wavelength $\lambda$ can be decreased by:
questions.solution:
The limit of resolution (minimum resolvable angle) of a telescope is:
$$\Delta\theta = \frac{1.22\lambda}{D}$$
To decrease the limit of resolution (and thereby increase the resolving power $\text{RP} = 1/\Delta\theta$), one must decrease the wavelength $\lambda$ and increase the diameter (aperture) $D$ of the objective.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A plane wavefront is incident on a thin convex lens. The emergent wavefront is:
options: Spherical and converging towards the focus
Spherical and diverging from the focus
questions.solution: A plane wave is transformed by a converging convex lens into a converging spherical wavefront whose centre of curvature coincides with the principal focus of the lens.

questions.question: If the distance between the source and a single slit is increased, the diffraction pattern on the screen:
options: Remains unchanged in fringe width, but intensity decreases
questions.solution:
The angular fringe width $\theta = \frac{\lambda}{a}$ and linear width $\beta = \frac{2\lambda D}{a}$ depend only on the wavelength $\lambda$, slit width $a$, and distance between the slit and the screen $D$.
Changing the distance between the primary source and the slit changes only the illuminance (intensity) of light entering the slit, leaving the width of diffraction fringes unaltered.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] In an interference experiment, the ratio of amplitudes of two coherent waves is $A_1 / A_2 = 3 / 2$. The ratio of maximum intensity to minimum intensity in the pattern is:
questions.solution:
Maximum and minimum intensities:
$$I_{\max} = (A_1 + A_2)^2, \quad I_{\min} = (A_1 - A_2)^2$$
$$\frac{I_{\max}}{I_{\min}} = \left(\frac{A_1 + A_2}{A_1 - A_2}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{3 + 2}{3 - 2}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{5}{1}\right)^2 = 25 : 1$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] Two polaroids are oriented with their transmission axes mutually perpendicular, so no light is transmitted. A third polaroid is introduced between them with its axis oriented at $45^\circ$ to both. If incident light on the first polaroid is unpolarised with intensity $I_0$, the transmitted intensity is:
questions.solution:
Intensity transmitted by polaroid 1: $I_1 = \frac{I_0}{2}$.
Intensity transmitted by middle polaroid 2 at $\theta_1 = 45^\circ$:
$$I_2 = I_1 \cos^2(45^\circ) = \frac{I_0}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{I_0}{4}$$
The angle between polaroid 2 and polaroid 3 is $\theta_2 = 90^\circ - 45^\circ = 45^\circ$:
$$I_3 = I_2 \cos^2(45^\circ) = \frac{I_0}{4} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{I_0}{8}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] In a Young's double slit experiment, slit separation is $d = 0.5\text{ mm}$ and screen distance is $D = 1.0\text{ m}$. If light of wavelength $500\text{ nm}$ is used, find the fringe width in millimetres.
questions.solution:
Fringe width formula:
$$\beta = \frac{\lambda D}{d}$$
Substitute $\lambda = 500 \times 10^{-9}\text{ m}$, $D = 1.0\text{ m}$, and $d = 0.5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}$:
$$\beta = \frac{(500 \times 10^{-9}\text{ m}) \times 1.0\text{ m}}{0.5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}} = \frac{5.0 \times 10^{-7}}{0.5 \times 10^{-3}} = 1.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m} = 1.0\text{ mm}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] In a single slit diffraction experiment, a slit of width $0.1\text{ mm}$ is illuminated by light of wavelength $600\text{ nm}$. Find the angular width (in milliradians) of the central diffraction maximum.
questions.solution:
Angular width of the central maximum:
$$2\theta = \frac{2\lambda}{a}$$
Substitute $\lambda = 600 \times 10^{-9}\text{ m}$ and $a = 0.1 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}$:
$$2\theta = \frac{2 \times (600 \times 10^{-9})}{0.1 \times 10^{-3}} = \frac{1.2 \times 10^{-6}}{10^{-4}} = 1.2 \times 10^{-2}\text{ rad} = 12.0\text{ mrad}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] In Young's double slit experiment, the distance between slits is $0.2\text{ mm}$ and the distance to the screen is $1.5\text{ m}$. If the distance between the central bright fringe and the $3^{\text{rd}}$ bright fringe is $13.5\text{ mm}$, find the wavelength of light in nanometers.
questions.solution:
Distance to the $n^{\text{th}}$ bright fringe:
$$y_n = n \frac{\lambda D}{d}$$
For $n = 3$, $y_3 = 13.5 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}$:
$$13.5 \times 10^{-3} = 3 \times \frac{\lambda \times 1.5}{0.2 \times 10^{-3}}$$
$$13.5 \times 10^{-3} = \lambda \times \frac{4.5}{0.2 \times 10^{-3}} = \lambda \times (2.25 \times 10^4)$$
$$\lambda = \frac{13.5 \times 10^{-3}}{2.25 \times 10^4} = 6.0 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m} = 600.0\text{ nm}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] In a Young's double slit experiment, a thin glass plate ($n = 1.5$) of thickness $6\,\mu\text{m}$ is introduced into the path of one of the beams. Taking $\lambda = 500\text{ nm}$, find the number of fringes by which the central fringe shifts on the screen.
questions.solution:
The number of fringes shifted is given by:
$$N = \frac{(\mu - 1)t}{\lambda}$$
Substitute $\mu = 1.5$, $t = 6 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}$, and $\lambda = 500 \times 10^{-9}\text{ m}$:
$$N = \frac{(1.5 - 1) \times (6 \times 10^{-6})}{500 \times 10^{-9}} = \frac{0.5 \times (6 \times 10^{-6})}{5 \times 10^{-7}} = \frac{3.0 \times 10^{-6}}{0.5 \times 10^{-6}} = 6.0$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Find the Brewster angle (polarising angle) in degrees for light incident from air onto the surface of a diamond having a refractive index $\mu = 2.414$ (take $\tan 67.5^\circ \approx 2.414$).
questions.solution:
By Brewster's Law:
$$\tan\theta_p = \mu$$
Given $\mu = 2.414$:
$$\theta_p = \tan^{-1}(2.414) = 67.5^\circ$$
